Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (CTO), Samir (Head Infra), Rachel (SecEng), Omar (PM)

Summary: quick security posture exploration for inference (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Primary concerns: PII handling, KMS integration, SSO/SAML mapping to RBAC, audit logs and retention, SOC2/ISO evidence. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of regulatory controls but wants validated failure modes and pricing impact.

Topics: SOC2/ISO coverage, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC roles, audit logs & retention windows, encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS options (bring-your-own-key), network topology (VPCs, peering, egress), on-prem checklist, rollout timeline and pilot success criteria.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro—i'm Maya, our AE on this account, with Ethan, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lina (Hightower CTO): doing well, thanks. we wanted to go over what controls you have around inference, especially since we'll be feeding customer PHI-ish data into models for redaction and customer support.
[00:18] Ethan (Redwood SE): absolutely. high level, we run three deployment modes—hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/vpc or on-prem. each has slightly different control surface. i can walk through specifics: SOC2 scope, sso, kms, audit logs, and network flow.
[00:31] Samir (Head Infra): just to flag, banking regulation means we need key custody guarantees. BYOK is a must for us. also we track data residency by region so logs/outputs cannot leave eu region.
[00:44] Maya: great, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. for our hosted offering we offer customer-managed key integration on some regions—we can share the exact list.
[00:55] Rachel (SecEng): can you describe what "BYOK" means operationally? like, do you ever see our plaintext key? where are keys stored, hsm?
[01:05] Ethan: we integrate with cloud KMS providers—kms hsm-backed stores. keys never leave the customer's cloud tenant in the private path; for dedicated we can either proxy keys or set up a customer-managed key in our cloud tenant with tight IAM. we don't hold plaintext; we use envelope encryption where possible.
[01:23] Omar (PM): and how about tokenization or PII redaction pre-inference? i.e., can we run a pre-processor that masks pii and keep raw logs out of your storage?
[01:33] Ethan: yes, you can run preprocessing in your VPC or client-side. Redwood supports prefix caching and optional request-level redaction. note that some telemetry exists for billing and debugging, but we can configure to avoid storing full inputs for certain customers.
[01:48] Lina: ok. SOC2 and ISO—do you have SOC 2 type II and ISO-27001? any audit reports we can see?
[01:56] Maya: we are SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 certified; i'll attach redacted evidence and a control matrix. also note some of our Private deployments are customer-managed for compliance reasons, and we provide an operations playbook.
[02:10] Rachel: how granular is your RBAC? we need role separation: engineers that can deploy models, others that can only read metrics, and a tiny group to access logs for forensics.
[02:20] Ethan: RBAC is role-based with groups and teams; we integrate with SSO via SAML or OIDC and support SCIM for provisioning. you can configure least privilege roles—there is also audit logging for role changes. we can show sample policies.
[02:35] Samir: on SSO, can we map SAML attributes to RBAC? we want department and tenant claims mapped.
[02:41] Ethan: yes, that's supported, we map saml attributes to roles. SCIM sync helps keep groups in sync. sometimes mapping drills need a small script if attributes are custom—we can pair on that.
[02:55] Lina: audit logs—what's retained, is it tamper-evident, and can we ship to our SIEM?
[03:03] Maya: audit logs include admin actions, model deploys, token usage with redaction controls, and system events. retention windows differ by plan; we can export logs to customer S3 or to your SIEM using syslog/event collector. tamper-evidence is achieved via append-only logs in Private; for Hosted and Dedicated we provide signed log archives.
[03:21] Rachel: signed archives—what format and how often? daily? weekly?
[03:25] Ethan: typically daily bundles with checksums + metadata. we can increase frequency for Dedicated tier.
[03:33] Omar: latency tradeoffs—if we do dedicated with BYOK, does crypto ops add noticeable latency to calls?
[03:40] Ethan: encryption/decryption for envelope keys is negligible relative to model inference time. the big latency factors are model size and batching. BYOK handshake is an initial crypto op per session—won't add per-token cost significantly.
[03:55] Lina: we have a compliance requirement to keep all request/response payloads for 90 days but only retain structured metadata for a year. is that doable?
[04:05] Maya: yes we can configure retention by data class: e.g., keep raw request/response zero days by default for Hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can set 90 days for raw and 365 for metadata. we'll need to document exactly where the data lives (region) to meet residency.
[04:20] Samir: for Private on-prem, what's the minimal infra required? from a network and compute perspective.
[04:27] Ethan: minimal: a few GPU nodes (depending on model), a control plane VM for the management agent, and an egress path for updates if you want automatic patches. we'll send a checklist: ports (443, 10250-ish for kube), outbound to our artifact registries optional, and an offline bundle if you're air-gapped.
[04:46] Rachel: air-gap/air-gapped deployment—can we get an on-prem bundle and then run vulnerability assessments locally?
[04:53] Ethan: yes, we have an offline installer and an SBOM; we also provide a hardened image and playbook for running local audits.
[05:03] Lina: one thing i worry about is fallback modes—if dedicated capacity hits limits or we lose a zone, what's the behavior?
[05:12] Maya: we provide automatic fallback policies: you can failover to a lower-capacity variant in the same region or route to a hosted fallback in another region depending on your tolerance. for strict compliance we can disable cross-region failover.
[05:25] Omar: auditors often ask for separation between dev/staging/prod keys and enrollments—can we have environment-scoped keys?
[05:33] Ethan: absolutely. keys can be scoped per environment and mapped to different RBAC groups. we recommend separate projects/tenants per environment to reduce blast radius.
[05:45] Rachel: any PII masking recommendations? we need patterns that don't break model performance.
[05:52] Ethan: we recommend deterministic tokenization for entities and preserve minimal context for tasks that need it. we also have post-processing filters and can run K-anonymity checks before storing. there is a trade-off, we'll help tune prompts and the pre-processing layer.
[06:08] Lina: do you allow obfuscation of logs so you can still get metrics but we avoid exposing raw text?
[06:15] Maya: yes, we redaction-tokensize metrics—there's an obfuscation mode that retains token counts and latency but replaces content with placeholders.
[06:24] Samir: what about encryption at-rest for model weights and caches (kv cache)? some providers keep kv cache unencrypted which is a no-go for us.
[06:34] Ethan: we encrypt model artifacts at rest and the KV cache; in Dedicated and Private options, cache encryption is BYOK-backed or tenant-managed. note that caching in memory is ephemeral and cleared on process restart.
[06:48] Rachel: compliance evidence: do you have a controls matrix mapping SOC2 controls to your product features?
[06:55] Maya: yes, that's part of the security pack i'll send; it maps controls to architecture diagrams and evidence snippets.
[07:04] Omar: timeline—if we wanted a pilot, what does success look like and how long?
[07:09] Maya: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: week 0 onboarding + network setup, week 1-2 performance and policies, week 3-4 integration + audit checks. success criteria: latency within x ms for p99, no data leakage in test prompts, SSO mapping functioning, and BYOK validated.
[07:28] Lina: cost—if we do Dedicated with reserved capacity vs private on-prem, ballpark delta?
[07:35] Maya: Dedicated has a hosting fee plus reserved GPU commit—cheaper ops than building everything yourself, Private has higher upfront integration and licensing. i'll put specific pricing in the follow-up.
[07:47] Samir: small technical nit—do you rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation cadence?
[07:53] Ethan: rotations can be automated, or you can trigger and manage rotations from your KMS. we support key versioning and graceful key rollover flows.
[08:02] Rachel: logs to SIEM—what events are included? we need admin changes, model deploys, API tokens issued/revoked, and anomalous usage alerts.
[08:11] Ethan: all those are standard events; anomalous usage alerts can be configured to push to your PagerDuty or Slack.
[08:18] Lina: last question—what's the escalation and incident response process for security incidents?
[08:24] Maya: we have a 24/7 security on-call for enterprise customers, incident playbooks, and we can commit to notif windows in our SLA. for Dedicated/Private we offer a faster on-call routing.
[08:36] Omar: great. that's helpful. next steps?
[08:40] Maya: i'll send the security pack, SOC2 artifacts, dedicated pricing, and an onboarding checklist. ethan will work with samir on the on-prem checklist. can we aim for next call the week of Aug 17?
[08:52] Lina: yes that works. thanks everyone.
